title: Dinosaur Provincial Park, Alberta
summary: Dinosaur Provincial Park in Alberta exposes Campanian strata of the Oldman and Dinosaur Park formations, dated by uranium-lead to 76.72–74.30 million years, laid down on alluvial to coastal plains west of the Bearpaw seaway. They yield over 166 vertebrate taxa, including 51 non-avian dinosaur species such as Gorgosaurus, Centrosaurus, Styracosaurus and Chasmosaurus.

uncertainty.note: U-Pb range for the strata from the IUGS geoheritage page. Argon dates on bentonites in the Dinosaur Park Formation give about 76.1 to 77.0 Ma (Campbell et al. 2016), so the two methods overlap but do not agree exactly.

beats.caption: Alluvial to coastal plains west of the Bearpaw seaway laid down the Oldman and Dinosaur Park formations in Campanian time.
Among over 166 vertebrate taxa are 51 non-avian dinosaur species; bonebeds hold hundreds of Centrosaurus, Coronosaurus or Styracosaurus.
More than 110 years of collecting has sent over 500 dinosaur specimens from the park to museums worldwide.
